reasoning_traces.think:
The core methodology combines topological data analysis (TDA) with graph theory to model tennis match dynamics. The lower-star filtration constructs a sequence of simplicial complexes from player performance data, capturing temporal trends via a weighted win rate function g(v). This enables persistent homology to extract stable topological signatures that reflect long-term dominance patterns. Simultaneously, a directed Katz similarity index computes asymmetric influence paths between players, incorporating recency-weighted historical outcomes. These two frameworks—TDA and graph theory—are unified through shared node-edge structures and temporal weighting schemes. The resulting features are fed into classifiers such as logistic regression, random forests, and XGBoost, which learn to map these topological and relational signals into match outcome predictions. The key insight is that both topological invariants and graph-based similarities encode complementary aspects of player dominance, enhancing predictive power beyond traditional ranking systems alone.
